events.title: Outside the Lecture Hall
events.summary: A disagreement turns public between two students.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Outside the lecture hall, a heated argument draws a crowd. One student is filming. Nobody looks sure how it started, but everyone has an opinion.

choices.label: Ask everyone to pause and move the conversation somewhere private.
Call a faculty member or campus security.
Take your friend and leave before the crowd gets involved.
Shout back and make yourself part of the confrontation.

calm.speaker: narrator
calm.text: The volume drops by degrees. It is not dramatic, but the crowd loses interest and the students agree to speak with a tutor.

security.speaker: narrator
security.text: A faculty member arrives and separates the students. You give a short account, then return to class.

leave.speaker: narrator
leave.text: You do not get the satisfaction of the last word. You do get to make it to your next lecture.

shout.speaker: narrator
shout.text: The argument becomes a spectacle. A tutor writes down your name, and your friend asks why you made a bad afternoon bigger.

events.title: The Extra Sheet
events.summary: An exam decision tests more than memory.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Ten minutes into the paper, a folded answer sheet appears under the edge of the desk behind you. Your friend catches your eye. The invigilator is checking the other side of the room.

choices.label: Hand it to the invigilator without opening it.
Leave it where it is and keep writing your own paper.
Use it. You are already behind and nobody may notice.
Quietly tell your friend to put it away and finish honestly.

report.speaker: narrator
report.text: The invigilator takes the sheet and asks you two calm questions. Your pulse settles; your paper is still yours.

ignore.speaker: narrator
ignore.text: You keep your eyes on your own work. The room becomes very quiet, but you finish with a clear conscience.

use.speaker: narrator
use.text: The answers save a few marks and cost you sleep. A later review notices the pattern, and your academic record now has a shadow.

warn.speaker: narrator
warn.text: Your friend folds the sheet back up. You both sit with the awkwardness and submit what you actually know.

events.title: One More Round
events.summary: A night out asks what kind of friend you want to be.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The bar is loud, the band is good, and someone at your table keeps ordering another round for everyone. Your friend has stopped looking comfortable.

choices.label: Order water and food for the table.
Call a cab and leave with your friend.
Join the round and let the night decide itself.
Say clearly that nobody should be pressured to drink.

water.speaker: narrator
water.text: The food arrives. Conversation comes back. The night is less cinematic and much easier to remember.

leave.speaker: narrator
leave.text: Outside, the air is cooler. Your friend thanks you for noticing before the night became a story they did not want.

join.speaker: narrator
join.text: The music blurs into a morning headache and an expensive card notification.

boundary.speaker: narrator
boundary.text: There is a brief awkward silence. Then another friend says, 'Good. I was waiting for someone to say it.'

events.title: Behind the Canteen
events.summary: A small social choice can become a habit.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A few classmates are taking a smoke break behind the canteen. Someone offers you one and says it is only about having a minute away from everybody else.

choices.label: Refuse and stay for the conversation.
Take a walk instead and return to class.
Try it once because you do not want to look nervous.
Ask why the group comes here and listen.

refuse.speaker: narrator
refuse.text: Nobody makes a speech about it. The conversation continues, which is useful information about how much pressure was really there.

walk.speaker: narrator
walk.text: You take the long way around the quad and arrive back with a clearer head.

try.speaker: narrator
try.text: The smoke is harsher than the movie version. The social part, unfortunately, is easy to repeat.

question.speaker: narrator
question.text: The answer is mostly stress and habit. Nobody seems proud of either one.

events.title: The Scout's Clipboard
events.summary: Practice begins to look like an opportunity.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A local club scout has watched you play twice. The offer is not glamorous: early practice, travel, and a chance to earn a small match fee.

choices.label: Commit to structured practice for a season.
Keep sport as a hobby while you focus on exams.
Ask about safety, schedule and what the fee really covers.
Decline kindly; the timing is not right.

commit.speaker: narrator
commit.text: The clipboard becomes a calendar. You are not a professional yet, but the path is no longer imaginary.

study.speaker: narrator
study.text: You keep your shoes by the door and your notes on the desk. The hobby stays yours, which is its own kind of success.

negotiate.speaker: narrator
negotiate.text: The scout respects the questions and returns with a clearer offer. Details matter when a dream gets paperwork.

decline.speaker: narrator
decline.text: The scout leaves a number in your phone. Some doors can wait without disappearing.

events.title: The Breaking Headline
events.summary: A market headline tests your patience.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A dramatic headline says the market is about to collapse. The fictional market board is down, but nobody knows whether the story is signal, panic, or a person trying to sell clicks.

choices.label: Check your time horizon and hold your plan.
Read the company notes before deciding anything.
Sell everything immediately.
Close the app and get on with your day.

hold.speaker: narrator
hold.text: The headline keeps shouting. Your plan is quieter, and that is why it survives the afternoon.

research.speaker: narrator
research.text: You find three facts, two opinions and one missing piece. Uncertainty feels less frightening when you name it.

panic.speaker: narrator
panic.text: The order goes through. Relief arrives first; the question of whether you acted too quickly arrives later.

ignore.speaker: narrator
ignore.text: The market will still be there tomorrow. Your friend, your class and your dinner also count as assets.
